summary: This file extracts metadata from MDX blog posts using Webpack's dynamic loading, parsing frontmatter (the metadata at the top of each file) to build a structured list of post information. It handles both English posts and French translations, allowing callers to include or exclude draft and unlisted posts as needed. The main `getBlogMetadata()` function reads raw post data, while `useBlogMetadata()` adds locale awareness by overlaying translated titles and descriptions for non-English pages.

explanations.47: This type says a blog tag can be either a simple string (like 'javascript') or an object with a label property—we accept both because different parts of the codebase use different formats.
explanations.65: Even though the frontmatter parser sometimes returns a real Date object, we declare this as string to match what existing code expects; JavaScript's Date constructor accepts both anyway.
explanations.101: The `!!` prefix is a Webpack loader instruction that forces the frontmatter-loader plugin to run instead of the default blog plugin, allowing us to capture draft posts that would otherwise be filtered out.
explanations.113: We create a separate context for French translations because the main context always reads from the English blog folder regardless of which language is being rendered.
explanations.127: We extract the folder name by removing the index file and leading dot, then use the slug from frontmatter if available, otherwise fall back to the last part of the directory path.
explanations.164: If a slug doesn't start with a slash, we prepend `/blog/` to create the full URL path; if it already starts with a slash, we use it as-is.
explanations.172: Relative image paths like `./image.png` are converted to absolute paths by inserting the blog post's directory, making them work from any page that links to the post.
explanations.191: This filters out null entries (files without titles, which aren't real articles) by using TypeScript's type guard—it tells TypeScript that whatever survives this check is definitely a BlogPostMetadata.
explanations.215: We call `useTranslationState()` to find out which locale we're rendering and whether posts have been translated into that locale.
explanations.217: The `filterTranslated()` helper keeps only posts that exist in the current locale's translated corpus, so French pages don't show untranslated articles.
explanations.227: We look up the translated title and description using the post's slug, and if they exist, we use them instead of the English versions.
